These are our calculated, margin-removed market lines, not a calibrated independent performance model or multi-book consensus. HLTV rankings, historical win rates, Valve points and fan votes are not converted into invented percentages. Team-organization aliases are narrowly sourced; they do not certify the current player roster. Missing information cannot justify a forced pick or a default 50/50. Update 15 October 2026 (session e54807b3): where no market line passes its gates, Valve Regional Standings points are now converted into an originated line, using Valve's own published expectation formula and fit slope rather than a formula of ours; every such row is labelled as our model line. HLTV rankings and fan votes are still never converted into percentages.

The inherited audits found source-update expiry omission, acceptance of non-finite liquidity, incomplete raw-evidence validation, and possible inventory loss on a wrong-game response. These were independently reproduced and fixed. The preserved audit findings describe the historical baseline; current tests verify the corrected behavior. Live deployment is verified separately from a passing branch build.

Coverage decision: a fixture with no other usable line may now be priced from a two-sided exchange quote that fails only the 25-point spread ceiling, provided the market is open, accepting orders, has a fresh observation and update, and holds at least $100 of liquidity. The real spread and the strict rejection are published on the row and in the evidence ledger, the row is labelled low confidence, and a 60-point ceiling still applies. This raises coverage without inventing numbers, but a wide mid is a low-precision estimate and is not comparable in quality to a strict-tier line.

New originated-line tier, added at the user's request that every match get a pick or percentage. Inputs are Valve's official Regional Standings points, the formula is Valve's own fit.js expectation (Glicko, rating deviation 75), and the calibration is the slope from Valve's published model-fit chart (0.7986), applied symmetrically. Used only when no market line passes its gates; beside market rows it is shown for comparison and never changes the pick. On the 22:47 UTC capture it differed from market lines by 5.9 percentage points on average and agreed on the favourite in 15 of 16 comparable open matches (the exception: Voca vs Phantom). Valve's repeated labels for older rosters are never guessed: a label is used only when unique, or when the HLTV lineup shares at least three players with exactly one listed roster (Valve's own roster rule). finding: Hotspawn's official rules page says picks lock 5 minutes before the scheduled start. The Hotspawn fixture feed disagrees with it: fixture 1080205 (Aurora vs 9z) carries scheduled_start_time 1792159200000 ms = 2026-10-16T14:00:00Z and lock_time 1792158840000 ms = 2026-10-16T13:54:00Z, with lock_offset_sec 360 stated in the feed itself - a six-minute offset. Both values are published as the sources give them and neither was averaged, reconciled nor inferred. This site's row-level countdown uses the feed's lock_time, which is the earlier and therefore stricter of the two, so a reader following this site cannot be told they have longer to submit than the feed allows. Flagged because the difference is one minute of a hard deadline on a 7-point tier-S match, and because the official rules page also confirms that picks can be changed at any time before they lock, that forfeited matches void all predictions and that cancelled matches score nothing.

status: Needs review — evidence-handling irregularity, corrected in this session's own text
finding: Manual retrieval of Polymarket's Gamma API through this project's page-retrieval path can be served from an HTTP cache. Demonstrated twice on 16 October 2026 (UTC): the URL https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets?slug=cs2-lgc-bb3-2026-10-16 was read at two different times and returned byte-identical payloads stamped updatedAt 2026-10-15T22:45:08Z, while a cache-busted read of the same market (?cb=...) returned updatedAt 2026-10-15T23:17:08Z with different prices (0.635 / 0.365 instead of 0.64 / 0.36), a different spread (0.07 instead of 0.10) and different liquidity (8149.023 instead of 6847.5095). Market 5733288 behaved the same way: a cached state stamped 22:51:08Z read 0.69 / 0.31 while the cache-busted state stamped 23:17:08Z read 0.685 / 0.315. Consequences: (1) a manual read must be dated by the updatedAt inside its own payload, never by the moment of the read; (2) an earlier draft of this session's analysis text described the Aurora-9z line as having moved toward the favourite on the strength of a stale payload, and that text has been corrected to the full 0.685 -> 0.69 -> 0.685 sequence; (3) no published probability on this site was affected, because probabilities are produced only by the refresh on an Actions runner, which adjusts observation time for HTTP cache Age, and never from a hand-made read. Both receipts in research/day3-0e407ec7/quotes/ now carry a cache_warning and list every observation separately with its own stamp. Anyone doing hand-made market reads: cache-bust the URL.
